knowledge_point.title: Calculating a Definite Integral of a Rational Function Using Substitution

question.:question/worked-solution:
We start by changing the variable:

$$
\begin{aligned}u & =4 x - 1 \\ \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =4 \\ \text{d}u & =4\,\text{d}x \\ \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u & =1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we create a table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=4 x - 1.$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & 1 & 3 \\ u & 3 & 11\end{aligned}
$$

So, the integral in terms of the new variable is

$$
\int_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{4 x - 1}\,\text{d}x=\int_{3}^{11}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u.
$$

Finally, we can solve it and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_{3}^{11}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{1}{4}\,\text{d}u & =\frac{1}{4}\int_{3}^{11}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\ln(u)|_{3}^{11} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\ln(11)-\ln(3)) \\  & =- \frac{\log{\left(3 \right)}}{4} + \frac{\log{\left(11 \right)}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

generation.domain: a*x^n+b>0 throughout closed original x interval; no poles
